mentions.name: Clor
mentions.description: A CLI that lets a coding agent create "claws" — background agents that automate anything on a schedule and run on a laptop, Mac mini, or a VM. A claw is defined and shared as a single CLAW.md file containing metadata (name, schedule, personality) and one or more ordered tasks, where each task is either a real agent run with full tool use or a plain bash step. Installing sets up the CLI, a small scheduling daemon, and a skill invocable from the agent (/claws in Claude Code or $claws in Codex).
mentions.problem: Existing agentic platforms the author tried (a hosting service on OpenClaw and self-run Hermes) failed more often than not at real work and had worrying security models; cron-style wake-work-sleep is an efficient pattern for "always on" tasks, and coding agents turned out to be the best tool for automating anything given the right environment and tools.
mentions.source_excerpt:
So I built Clor, a CLI that lets your coding agent create "claws", which are background agents that automate anything on a schedule and run on your laptop, Mac mini, or a VM.

https://clor.com
